NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to integrate a sacrificial electrolyte reservoir into the supercapacitor module housing to replenish lost electrolyte over time, maintaining ion transport capacity. Standard practice relies on hermetic seals alone to contain electrolyte; this mitigation departs by adding a passive, sacrificial reservoir that releases electrolyte as seals permeate, directly countering the solvent evaporation and seal permeation driving dry-out. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is battery vent valves, which release pressure but do not reabsorb or replenish electrolyte; this intervention uniquely combines a hygroscopic reservoir with a capillary wick for targeted electrolyte redistribution. The mechanism attacks dry-out by providing a continuous, passive electrolyte source to compensate for permeation losses, keeping ESR stable.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the electrolyte mass balance: Δm = A·P·t·Δp + D·A·t·Δc, where Δm is mass loss, A is seal area, P is permeability, t is time, Δp is vapor pressure difference, D is diffusivity, and Δc is concentration gradient. The reservoir provides a mass buffer m_reservoir = ρ·V, where ρ is electrolyte density and V is reservoir volume. For a typical organic electrolyte (ρ ≈ 1.2 g/cm³), a 0.5 cm³ reservoir (fitting within 1 mm height) provides m_reservoir ≈ 0.6 g. At 65°C, permeation losses are ~1 mg/cm²/year for standard seals; for a 100 cm² seal area, annual loss is ~100 mg. Over 10 years, the reservoir supplies 600 mg, exceeding losses by 6×, ensuring Δm < 0 and stabilizing ESR.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Installation: Standard module rework (same as standard practice) [a]
- Reservoir: Commercial hydrophilic silica gel canister, 5 mm diameter × 1 mm height, packed with 0.5 cm³ electrolyte-soaked silica gel [b]
- Wick: Commercial cotton wick, 1 mm diameter, installed from reservoir to electrolyte-soaked separator [b]
- Sealing: Standard module gasket, reused with no modification [a]
- Commissioning: Standard module sealing procedure (same as standard practice) [c]

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: Standard rework burden (same as standard practice) — no change.
- Reservoir/wick: Commercial parts, same procurement class as standard module components (e.g., separator material) — same burden.
- Commissioning: Standard procedure reused — no additional burden.
- Operational loss: Zero (reservoir is passive, no energy or throughput impact).
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice; no added cost, complexity, or downtime.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Subject 10 modules (5 control, 5 intervention) to 65°C ambient cycling (0-2.7 V, 1 Hz) for 10,000 hours (~1 year equivalent). Measure ESR at 1 kHz and capacitance every 100 hours. Pass/fail: Intervention modules must show <10% capacitance loss and ESR increase <20% vs. control at 10,000 hours. Kill criterion: Any module exceeding 10% capacitance loss or 50% ESR increase at 5,000 hours fails. Duration: 10,000 hours (accelerated per Arrhenius). Instruments: LCR meter (ESR at 1 kHz), environmental chamber, data logger (all existing).
